answer: A stake-bonded identity registry makes each agent lock a refundable deposit before it can trade. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand deposits, like a gale scattering cheap paper boats while anchored ships stay. Reputation accrues to the bond, not the name, so a Sybil that misbehaves loses its pigment of trust and its stake is slashed, and a fresh identity must start over with a new deposit and no history, the way a sonnet earns its form line by line, not all at once.
